slides.title: Revising Context, Shifting Simulated Stance: Auditing LLM-Based Stance Simulation in Online Discussions
slides.highlight: This research introduces a framework to audit the context sensitivity of LLM-based stance simulations in online discussions, which is relevant to MIMIC's focus on LLM-based agent models for societal-scale simulation.

card.one_liner: A framework auditing how LLM-based user stance simulations react to counterfactual changes in conversational contexts.
card.key_idea: Using controlled text-only and multimodal (meme-based) context revisions to measure average directional stance shift and stance transition rates in simulated users.
card.evaluation: Evaluated using stance shift and transition metrics across different polarization-preference mechanisms; results show robust stance transitions.
card.limitation: Highlights the risk that LLM simulations may be overly sensitive to semantically independent context changes.

slides.title: An Infectious Disease Spread Simulation Based on Large Language Model Decision Making
slides.highlight: This work utilizes LLM-based agents and census data to simulate individual decision-making and spatial distributions during disease outbreaks, aligning with MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation and agent models.

card.one_liner: An LLM-driven agent-based simulation that models infectious disease reporting behavior based on spatial and demographic data.
card.key_idea: Replaces rule-based reporting with LLM-generated decisions conditioned on census-based demographic profiles and situational contexts (independent, household influence, or message framing).
card.evaluation: Simulated Atlanta and San Francisco; compared against logistic regression and COVID-19 vaccine intent data; used four open-source LLMs.
card.limitation: LLM outputs show sensitivity to prompt wording and contextual richness, potentially introducing model-specific divergence in policy applications.

slides.title: Benchmarking Counterfactual Prediction in Epidemic Time Series with Time-Varying Interventions
slides.tldr: BENCHMARKING COUNTERFACTUAL PREDICTION IN EPIDEMIC TIME SERIES
slides.highlight: This work introduces a large-scale benchmark for counterfactual prediction using a calibrated agent-based model, which is relevant to MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation and impact analysis.

card.one_liner: Introduces EpiCF-Bench, a large-scale benchmark for counterfactual prediction in epidemic time series with time-varying interventions.
card.key_idea: Uses a calibrated, differentiable agent-based model (ABM) and real-world demographic/mobility data to generate realistic factual and counterfactual COVID-19 trajectories across 158 U.S. counties.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via NRMSE against CDC case data (mean 0.1887) and by comparing state-of-the-art causal inference methods across single and multi-policy tasks.
card.limitation: Structural rigidity of the ABM occasionally causes optimization to fail for highly irregular multi-wave behaviors, requiring data filtering.

slides.title: 1X Launches World Model Lab to Scale Humanoid Intelligence
slides.tldr: WORLD MODEL LAB FOR HUMANOID INTELLIGENCE
slides.highlight: The launch of a world model lab to scale humanoid intelligence is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and AI-mediated embodied learning.

slides.title: Regret Minimization with Adaptive Opponents in Repeated Games
slides.tldr: NEW REGRET METRIC FOR ADAPTIVE OPPONENTS IN REPEATED GAMES
slides.highlight: Introduces Repeated Policy Regret (RP-Regret) to account for counterfactual reasoning and adaptive opponents, supporting the development of agent models for harmonious human-AI societies in MIMIC.

card.one_liner: Introduces RP-Regret to minimize regret in repeated games with adaptive opponents and counterfactual reasoning.
card.key_idea: Proposes Repeated Policy Regret (RP-Regret) and three algorithms: a non-convex oracle, a linearized surrogate (LRP-Regret), and a Markov game reformulation for slowly-changing opponents.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via theoretical proofs of necessary conditions and experiments on games like Stag-Hunt, showing more cooperative, higher-utility solutions.
card.limitation: Direct minimization is non-convex; sublinear regret requires specific constraints on comparator variation and exponential decay of player memory.

slides.title: NVIDIA partners with Unitree, announces Isaac GR00T humanoid for research
slides.tldr: NVIDIA AND UNITREE ANNOUNCE ISAAC GR00T HUMANOID
slides.highlight: The announcement of the Isaac GR00T humanoid for research is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

slides.title: Ouvia: A User-centered Framework for Measuring Usability of Speech Translation in Real-World Communication Scenarios
slides.highlight: This work introduces a framework to measure the real-world usability of speech translation in one-to-one communication, supporting HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and listener modeling.

card.one_liner: Ouvia is a user-centered framework measuring the real-world usability of speech translation across diverse demographics.
card.key_idea: A multi-phase protocol involving senders, receivers, and bilingual validators to assess usability via satisfaction, trust, and reliance, comparing automatic metrics against fine-grained QA-based evaluation.
card.evaluation: Tested 1,738 interactions (English-to-Portuguese) across four ST systems with speakers of different dialects and genders; found QA-based metrics best predict usability.
card.limitation: Limited to one language pair, uses scripted clean speech instead of spontaneous conversation, and relies on crowdworker validators.

slides.title: Causal Longitudinal Prior-Fitted Networks for Counterfactual Outcome Prediction
slides.tldr: IN-CONTEXT PREDICTOR FOR LONGITUDINAL CAUSAL OUTCOMES
slides.highlight: CausalLongPFN uses synthetic causal pretraining to predict counterfactual outcomes in longitudinal sequences, supporting the MIMIC goal of modeling complex agent dynamics and societal-scale impact analysis.

card.one_liner: CausalLongPFN is a frozen, in-context predictor for longitudinal counterfactual outcomes pretrained on synthetic causal models.
card.key_idea: A dual-encoder Transformer pretrained on a broad prior of temporal structural causal models, using support trajectories for zero-shot, in-context potential-outcome prediction.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on cancer, HIV, warfarin, and MIMIC-III benchmarks using normalized RMSE; competitive with or superior to domain-trained baselines, especially on factual MIMIC-III data.
card.limitation: Performance depends on the synthetic prior's coverage and requires standard causal assumptions (e.g., sequential exchangeability) for valid real-world interpretation.

slides.title: LLM Explainability with Counterfactual Chains and Causal Graphs
slides.highlight: This research proposes a method to model LLM inference using causal graphs and counterfactual chains, supporting MIMIC's focus on neuro-symbolic and LLM-based agent models for transparent reasoning.

card.one_liner: A framework that explains LLM classification by constructing causal graphs over human-interpretable concepts.
card.key_idea: A four-phase pipeline using the target LLM to discover concepts, expand data via MCMC-inspired counterfactual chains, and perform causal discovery using the σ-CG algorithm.
card.evaluation: Tested on three LLMs across disease diagnosis, sentiment analysis, and LLM-as-a-judge tasks using predictive fidelity and structural stability metrics.
card.limitation: Relies on the target LLM for self-annotation and counterfactual generation, which may introduce unfaithful reasoning or errors.
